title: Michael Mann
summary: American director of night-city crime films — Thief, Heat, Collateral — obsessed with professionals and procedure.

related.note: Los Angeles at night, shot largely on digital video.

title: Tangerine Dream
summary: German electronic group whose sequencer-driven scores for Thief, Sorcerer and others shaped synth soundtracks.

title: Collateral
summary: Michael Mann’s 2004 thriller: a cab driver, a hitman and one long night across Los Angeles.

title: Drive
summary: Nicolas Winding Refn’s 2011 film about a stunt driver who works nights as a getaway driver; neon, silence and a synth-pop soundtrack.

title: Nicolas Winding Refn
summary: Danish director of Drive, Only God Forgives and the Pusher trilogy; known for neon-saturated, near-silent films.

title: Cliff Martinez
summary: Former drummer for Red Hot Chili Peppers turned film composer; his glassy synth score is half of Drive’s atmosphere.

title: OutRun
summary: Sega’s 1986 arcade driving game — a convertible, a coastline and a choice of radio station.

title: Hyperdub
summary: London label founded by Kode9; home to Burial and a lineage of experimental UK bass music.

title: Mamoru Oshii
summary: Japanese director of Ghost in the Shell and Patlabor 2, known for slow, philosophical, city-obsessed films.

title: Kenji Kawai
summary: Composer of Ghost in the Shell’s choral score and many Oshii films.

title: Sega Dreamcast
summary: Sega’s final home console (1998 in Japan); built-in modem, inventive games, discontinued in 2001.

related.note: Jet Set Radio launched on Dreamcast.
Sega’s NAOMI arcade board was built on Dreamcast-like hardware.

title: Hideki Naganuma
summary: Sega composer behind Jet Set Radio’s sample-heavy funk and hip-hop sound.

title: Smilebit
summary: Sega’s internal studio behind Jet Set Radio and Panzer Dragoon Orta.

title: Rival Schools: United by Fate
summary: Capcom’s 1997 team-based fighting game set in rival Japanese high schools.

title: Sega NAOMI
summary: Sega’s 1998 arcade platform, closely related to the Dreamcast; it ran many late-90s and 2000s arcade games.

title: Capcom
summary: Osaka developer of Street Fighter, Darkstalkers and Rival Schools — the center of arcade fighting game history.

related.note: Capcom’s CP System II board powered its mid-90s fighters.

title: CP System II
summary: Capcom’s 1993 arcade board behind Super Street Fighter II, the Alpha series, Darkstalkers and more.

title: Samurai Champloo
summary: Shinichirō Watanabe’s 2004 series: Edo-period Japan scored with hip-hop.

related.note: Nujabes was one of its composers.

title: Shinichirō Watanabe
summary: Japanese director whose anime are built around music: Cowboy Bebop, Samurai Champloo, Space Dandy.

title: Cowboy Bebop
summary: 1998 series about bounty hunters in space, scored by Yoko Kanno’s jazz band the Seatbelts.

related.note: Music by Yoko Kanno and the Seatbelts.

title: Yoko Kanno
summary: Composer of Cowboy Bebop’s jazz, blues and big-band soundtrack, performed by the Seatbelts.

title: Shing02
summary: Japanese-American MC and producer, longtime Nujabes collaborator.

title: Madlib
summary: Oxnard, California producer and crate-digger; half of Madvillain with MF DOOM.

title: MF DOOM
summary: Masked rapper and producer; Madvillainy with Madlib is one of underground hip-hop’s landmark albums.

title: Blue Note Records
summary: The jazz label whose 1950s–60s catalog became a deep well for hip-hop samples.

title: J Dilla
summary: Detroit producer whose loose, off-grid drums changed hip-hop; his MPC3000 is in the Smithsonian.

title: Nigo
summary: Founder of A Bathing Ape; later co-founded Billionaire Boys Club and became Kenzo’s artistic director.

title: Pharrell Williams
summary: Producer and designer who brought BAPE into American hip-hop and co-founded Billionaire Boys Club with Nigo.

title: Nike Air Force 1
summary: Bruce Kilgore’s 1982 basketball shoe — the template for the Bapesta and countless others.

title: Berserk
summary: Kentaro Miura’s dark fantasy manga, begun in 1989.

title: Katsuhiro Otomo
summary: Manga artist and director of Akira.

title: Hayao Miyazaki
summary: Studio Ghibli co-founder and director; admirer and friend of Moebius.

title: Madhouse
summary: Tokyo animation studio behind Ninja Scroll, Perfect Blue and many classics.

title: Archive Team
summary: Volunteer group that rescues websites before they shut down — GeoCities included.

title: Neocities
summary: Free static web hosting in the spirit of GeoCities, founded in 2013.

title: Internet Archive
summary: Nonprofit digital library founded in 1996; runs the Wayback Machine.

related.note: The Wayback Machine is its web archive.

title: Style Wars
summary: 1983 documentary by Tony Silver and Henry Chalfant about New York subway graffiti and early hip-hop.

related.note: Chalfant’s photographs and film document the same scene.
